text:
The only failing spec is slew rate, at 9.7 MV/s against a 10 MV/s target. It is limited by the tail current: Itail has by far the largest sensitivity (+10.2% per +10%).

The tail device M5 is also at the edge of saturation, with only 16 mV of margin. That is why the tail delivers about 37 µA instead of the intended 40 µA.

Two changes address both problems:
- **Raise Itail.** This gives slew margin. It also restores the full tail current once M5 sits properly in saturation.
- **Lower gmid1.** A lower gm/Id on the input pair raises its Vgs, which raises the tail node voltage and gives M5 more headroom.

A slightly larger Cc keeps phase margin, since UGBW rises with the extra input-pair current. Power stays around 0.6 mW, within the 1 mW limit.

```json
{"action": "refine",
 "reason": "Only slew fails; it is tail-current limited and M5 is at the edge of saturation. Raise Itail, lower gmid1 to give M5 headroom, and raise Cc slightly to hold PM.",
 "params": {"Itail": 56e-6, "gmid1": 12.0, "Cc": 3.4e-12, "I7": 260e-6, "kRz": 1.5},
 "bounds": {"Itail": [45e-6, 80e-6], "gmid1": [10.0, 15.0], "Cc": [2.5e-12, 4.5e-12]}}
```
